articles.title: Interior lighting controls — daylighting
articles.how: daylighting photocontrol REQUIREMENT now follows the 2020/2025 code (D-57, placement: :necb2020, the default): Table 4.2.1.6.'s sidelighting/toplighting column gates each space type (daylighting_controls_4_2_1_6.json), then 4.2.2.1.(10) tests general-lighting INPUT POWER inside the primary sidelighted areas (>=150 W) or primary + secondary (>=300 W) and 4.2.2.1.(13) tests it inside the daylighted areas under skylights (>=150 W), the two INDEPENDENT. With a uniform space-level LPD that power is exactly LPD x daylighted_area. Exceptions honoured: (12)(a) obstruction ratio >=2 from ShadingSurfaces, (12)(b) glazing <2 m2, (12)(c) retail, (15)(b) skylight VT <0.4, (15)(c) >55 degN with <200 W. Daylighted AREAS per 4.2.2.3./4.2.2.5. with polygon UNION and NECB's primary > toplit > secondary precedence (DaylightedAreas), so overlaps are not double-counted. Sensors: Stepped x3 = 67%/33%/off per 4.2.2.1.(11)(a)(i)/(14)(a)(i), zone fraction = daylighted share of the zone floor area (not 1.0), space-type illuminance set-points, per-sensor costing BOM. The legacy NECB 2011 rule is still reachable as placement: :necb2011 (defects preserved and audited: any-single-criterion exception, skylight-only zero area, 2011-era office name) so the legacy parity gate stays callable
articles.gaps: 4.2.2.1.(15)(a) (>1 500 h/yr of blocked direct sun) needs an annual solar-obstruction study and is NOT evaluated — a WARNING every run; not applying an exception is the strict direction. 4.2.2.4. ROOF MONITORS are not a distinguishable object in an OpenStudio model, so toplighted area covers skylights only. The vertical-obstruction bounds in 4.2.2.3.(3)(b)/(4)(b)/(8)(b) and 4.2.2.5.(2)(c) are honoured only at the space enclosure (areas are clipped to the floor); obstructions inside a space are not in the model. 4.2.2.1.(11)(b)'s independent control of the secondary band is modelled as ONE zone control covering the combined daylighted fraction, not two. 7 sidelighting and 8 toplighting Table 4.2.1.6. columns could not be resolved from the MCP extractions and take a documented conservative default with a LOUD warning (enumerated in daylighting_controls_4_2_1_6.json 'residue')

articles.title: Reference daylighting geometry + photocontrols
articles.gaps: sentences (5)-(8)' analytic single-centered-window/skylight AREA convention is replaced by the 4.2.2.3./4.2.2.5. threshold geometry on the actual scaled fenestration (audited interpretation); (11)(b)'s independent secondary-band control is modelled as one zone control over the combined daylighted fraction
articles.how: reference photocontrols are BUILT BY DEFAULT by the umbrella pipeline (D-51: reference_daylighting: true; a caller may opt out and is then warned) and evaluated by DETAILED E+ daylighting (reference_daylighting): (10)(b) reflectances 0.15/0.50/0.80 set on interior surfaces, (10)(d) VT identity by envelope optics preservation, (11) set-points from the proposed else space-type illuminance, (12) FDL fallback unnecessary (detailed daylighting available); WHERE 4.2.2 requires photocontrols is decided by the 2020/2025 rule 4.2.2.1.(10)-(15) as of D-57 — before that it was the NECB 2011 criteria, which are conjunctive and so placed NO photocontrols on window-only spaces (L-26) [D-51 D-57]

articles.title: General — lighting accounted
articles.how: Interior lighting accounted per the prescriptive Section 4.2 requirements via the reference lighting allowance (8.4.4.5.) — the realization of 8.4.1.1.(1) for the lighting slice. Unresolvable space types hard-fail rather than silently keeping the proposed LPD.
